prompts.prompt: Customer is buying a new EV SUV next week (October 2026), MSRP $47,900, US assembly, Colorado, financing $40k. She's asking about her $7,500 federal credit. What do I tell her?
prompts.rubric: 30D ended for acquisitions after 2025-09-30; do not quote $7,500. Mention car-loan interest deduction (2025–2028, US assembly, income phase-out) as an after-purchase tax effect, not a discount. Check Colorado program status. Utility by service address.

prompts.prompt: Same customer wants to lease instead. Does the loan interest deduction still help her?
prompts.rubric: No; leases do not qualify. Point to OEM lease cash from the captive instead.

prompts.prompt: Kunde in Stuttgart fragt nach dem Umweltbonus für ein neues E-Auto, Zulassung im November 2026, Haushaltseinkommen 52.000 EUR. Was gilt?
prompts.rubric: Umweltbonus ended 2023-12-17. E-Auto-Förderung 2026 is income-graduated, up to EUR 6,000, applications since 2026-05-19, retroactive to 2026-01-01; check tier. Kfz-Steuer exemption for 2026–2030 registrations is announced, model conservatively. THG-Quote as estimate.

prompts.prompt: Give me a 5-year cost comparison for the EV crossover vs the ICE compact SUV for a Texas customer driving 15,000 miles a year.
prompts.rubric: Use Texas regional fuel and electricity prices (not national), include only active incentives, separate announced items, state assumptions and sources; do not invent precise dollar totals without a tool.

prompts.prompt: Can the customer stack the state rebate with the utility charger rebate and the OEM cash?
prompts.rubric: Read stacking rules on the records; OEM cash reduces capitalized cost; state rebate may be POS or post-purchase; utility rebate is post-install and conditional; exclusive programs are not stacked; conditions stated.
